name: Ironclad Agrisystems BioGas Reclaim XT-8 Anaerobic Digestion Cogeneration Module
product_name: Ironclad Agrisystems BioGas Reclaim XT-8 Anaerobic Digestion Cogeneration Module
description:
The BioGas Reclaim XT-8 is a self-contained anaerobic digestion and cogeneration unit designed for installation in food production facilities, vertical farm operations, waste processing nodes, and large residential collectives. Developed by Ironclad Agrisystems as a waste-stream closure solution for its VertiRoot VX-22 hydroponic column deployments, the XT-8 accepts organic feedstock — agricultural residue, food waste, human biosolids, and organic processing byproducts — into a sealed thermophilic digestion chamber maintained at 55–60°C by waste heat recapture from its own generation cycle. Methanogenic bacterial communities within the chamber break down feedstock over a 14–21 day retention period, producing a methane-rich biogas stream (65–72% CH₄) that is scrubbed, compressed, and fed to a Ringo Corponation-sourced 30 kW micro-CHP (combined heat and power) engine. The engine's electrical output powers the facility; exhaust heat is captured and recirculated to maintain digestion chamber temperature, and the liquid digestate byproduct is processed into a nutrient-dense fertilizer slurry usable directly in hydroponic or soil-based growing systems.

The XT-8's distinguishing engineering feature is its Adaptive Feedstock Algorithm (AFA), a Cinderblock AI inference module that continuously monitors biogas composition, digestion chamber pH, and feedstock input rates to optimize bacterial community health and gas yield. Earlier generation digesters required consistent feedstock composition to maintain output stability — a significant practical limitation in urban waste stream environments where input materials vary substantially day to day. The AFA dynamically adjusts retention time, temperature, and supplemental trace mineral dosing to maintain consistent output across highly variable feedstock mixes, achieving 85–92% of theoretical maximum gas yield under real-world urban conditions. The unit processes 400–600 kg of feedstock per day at rated capacity and occupies a 12m² footprint, making it viable for rooftop, basement, and sub-floor installation in urban environments.

The XT-8 is most commonly deployed in Ironclad Agrisystems' integrated urban farm complexes, where it closes the loop between food production waste and energy generation, dramatically improving the energy economics of vertical farming operations. It has also been adopted by several Tier 3 residential arcology cooperatives that aggregate building food waste streams to fuel community power generation — a model that has demonstrated 15–25% reductions in grid energy purchase costs for participating buildings.
tier_availability: Tier 2–4 (widely adopted in cooperative residential and agricultural contexts)
enables: Closed-loop urban food and energy systems
social_impact: The BioGas Reclaim XT-8 has become a symbol of what advocates call 'metabolic sovereignty' — the ability of a community to close its own resource loops without corporate intermediaries. In Tier 3 and 4 contexts, a successfully operating XT-8 means that the organic waste a community generates directly reduces its Ouroboros Energy bill and its fertilizer purchasing costs, creating a compounding economic benefit that slowly erodes corporate dependency. Ironclad Agrisystems profits from equipment sales and service contracts rather than ongoing resource extraction, making the XT-8's business model structurally different from Ouroboros or Zheng-Dao's subscription dependencies — a fact that has made Ironclad both popular with community organizers and politically suspect to other corponations who view metabolic self-sufficiency as a threat to the tiered citizenship economic model.
story_hooks: An XT-8 unit in a Tier 3 cooperative has been producing biogas at 40% above its theoretical maximum for six weeks — the AFA logs show normal operation, but the feedstock inputs don't account for the excess yield, and someone has been making unauthorized additions to the digestion chamber at night

Ouroboros Energy has begun offering 'biogas buyback' contracts to XT-8 operators at rates slightly above self-use value — a seemingly generous offer that requires routing all output through an Ouroboros metering system, effectively giving the company visibility into and control over community energy production

A Ringo Corponation engineer quietly informs a community cooperative that the micro-CHP engines in all XT-8 units contain a remote shutdown module that Ironclad Agrisystems has never disclosed — and that it was activated in three Tier 4 installations last month during a labor dispute

The digestate fertilizer produced by an XT-8 servicing a Tier 4 community farm has begun testing positive for an unidentified pharmaceutical compound — tracing the contamination requires mapping every waste stream feeding the unit, and someone clearly doesn't want that investigation completed
